raw_findings.text: The fence regex in extract_json uses double backslashes (r"\\(?:json)?...") instead of backticks, so it never matches a markdown code fence. The json_objects fallback still finds the JSON, but the fence optimization is dead code. Fence regex uses \\ instead of backticks, so code-fence matching never fires. Restore backticks and non-greedy matching in the fence regex: r"```(?:json)?\s*(\{.*?\})\s*```"
The json_objects docstring contains a literal tab character (\t) where "text" was intended: "Every top-level {...} in \text, by brace matching". Docstring has a literal tab where "text" was meant.

The new `json_objects` function treats any `{` outside a string as a potential object start, but it does not handle single-quoted strings. A stray `{` inside a single-quoted JSON-like snippet in prose could still trigger a false parse attempt. json_objects ignores single-quoted strings, may mis-scan prose with single quotes. Extend the string-state machine to track single quotes as well as double quotes, or document that only double-quoted strings are protected.

`PROVIDER_REQUEST_OPTIONS` is defined after `build_provider_chain` but the function's docstring says callers must read it from there. A caller that imports the module and calls `build_provider_chain` before the module finishes executing (unlikely but possible in tests) would see an empty dict. PROVIDER_REQUEST_OPTIONS defined after the function that documents it as the single source. Move the PROVIDER_REQUEST_OPTIONS definition above build_provider_chain.

The shebang line uses `python3` which may not exist on all systems (e.g., Windows without py launcher). The script is invoked via `python scripts/hare_local.py` in the docs, so the shebang is decorative. Shebang assumes python3 in PATH; not portable to Windows. Change shebang to `#!/usr/bin/env python3` for better portability.

The catch may never trigger. TimeoutError catch may not match urllib's actual exception type. Catch `urllib.error.URLError` and inspect `isinstance(e.reason, socket.timeout)` or catch `socket.timeout` directly.
